title: fix(fields): a currency grid column's width is its currency's minor unit, never an authored scale; a hydrated currency column's scale is reported (objectui#10783)
body:
Fixes #10783
Clause-②: no — the report this adds is a console warning and refuses nothing; no objectui accept set moves. The grid stops reading a currency column's `scale` to match the refusal `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 already ships. (The claim carried `no (narrowing)`; the dispatch asked for a re-judge on the built diff, and a warning-only report reads `no`.)

## What changed

**`GridField` (`@object-ui/fields`): the minor unit decides, never the column's `scale`.** `currencyWidth` read `c.scale` first, so an authored `scale` on a `currency` column beat the currency's ISO 4217 minor unit on both faces: the width a computed amount is stored at (`computeRow` through `storedFractionScale`) and the places the cell shows (`currencyText`). It now takes the resolved currency only. `scale` on a `number` column is unchanged. The docblocks that said an authored `scale` still decides (`GridColumn.scale`, `currencyWidth`, `storedFractionScale`, `currencyText`) now say the opposite and why.

The installed spec was re-measured first, on the published `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 this tree resolves:

| input | 17.5.0 |
|---|---|
| `InlineGridColumnSchema` `{ name, type: 'currency', scale: 2 }` | refused at `scale` |
| `InlineGridColumnSchema` `{ name, type: 'currency' }` | parses |
| `InlineGridColumnSchema` `{ name: 'amount', scale: 2 }` (identity-only) | **parses** |
| `InlineGridColumnSchema` `{ name, type: 'number', scale: 2 }` | parses |
| `FieldSchema` `{ type: 'currency', scale: 2 }` | refused at `scale` |
| `FormViewSchema` `subforms: [{ childObject, columns: [{ name, type: 'currency', scale: 2 }] }]` | **parses** (`columns` is `z.array(z.any())`) |

**The hydrated case: reported where the child field is known (`@object-ui/plugin-form`).** An identity-only column over a currency child field keeps parsing, because `hydrateColumns` fills its `type` at render time. The dispatch's default was that `objectui validate` reports it. Measured: it cannot know the child field's type.

- `objectui validate` judges one UI-schema document through `safeValidateSchema` (`@object-ui/types/zod`). On an `object-form`, `subforms[].columns` is `z.array(z.any())`, so `{ name: 'amount', type: 'currency', scale: 2 }`, `{ name: 'amount', scale: 2 }` and a bogus `{ zzz_not_a_key: 1 }` column all read VALID. The positive control in the same shape fires: `childObject: 5` is refused at `subforms.0.childObject`, so the zero is a reading, not a validator that never reached `subforms`.
- `inlineColumns` is not an objectui authoring key at all: it is `@objectstack/spec` field metadata on the child object's relationship field, relayed by `attachInlineSubforms` into `subforms[].columns`.
- The child object's fields are not in the document `objectui validate` reads; `childObject` is a name, resolved at runtime through `dataSource.getObjectSchema`.

So the report takes the dispatch's fallback: the nearest loud channel, a render-time diagnostic in the existing column-hydration path. `hydrateColumns` is the first place the child field is known. A column that resolves to `currency` and carries an authored `scale` gets one `console.warn` per column per page load (the `sectionFields.ts` dedupe convention), naming the column, the child object and whether the type was hydrated or declared. Its first sentence is the spec's refusal with the same subject. The declared arm is covered too, because a form view's `subforms[].columns` reaches this function unjudged by the spec. Nothing is refused and the column still renders, at its currency's minor unit. No new gate.

**Fixtures.** The two objectui#10355 pins that asserted an authored `scale` winning are replaced by the objectui#10783 pins, following that file's own precedent comment for a retired row; the first half of the display row (a stored amount with more places shows at the yen's width) stays. A `GridField.test.tsx` fixture declared `type: 'currency'` with `scale: 2`, which 17.5.0 refuses; its assertions never read the key (no currency resolved), so the key is gone.

**Changesets.** `.changeset/10783-grid-currency-scale-not-read.md` (`@object-ui/fields` minor with a Behaviour change note, `@object-ui/plugin-form` patch). The objectui#10355 changeset is still pending in this release and says an authored currency `scale` decides; it gets a dated note, as objectui#11073 did for the same file.

Draft PR objectui#11069 is untouched: this diff edits no `packages/cli` file.

## Tests

All readings at `587c35168` with a clean tree, root-form `pnpm exec vitest run` (no `--`), heavy runs through the shared verify lock.

| run | files | tests |
|---|---|---|
| the five touched test files, `--reporter=verbose` | 5 passed | 110 passed (13 of them in the two new pin files) |
| `packages/fields/` (three shards) | 225 passed, 1 skipped (226) | 3502 passed, 7 skipped |
| `packages/plugin-form/` (two shards) | 154 passed (154) | 1777 passed, 1 skipped |
| root `scripts/__tests__/` (two shards; this diff edits markdown) | 177 passed, 2 skipped (179) | 5371 passed, 2 skipped |

Type-check: the closure first, `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-form^...' --concurrency=2` (it contains `@object-ui/fields`), exit 0, 11 tasks. Then `type-check` for `@object-ui/fields` exit 0 and for `@object-ui/plugin-form` exit 0; both run `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and `--listFiles` on each test program lists the new pin files (fields 2 of the two currency pin files, plugin-form 1).

The pins:

- `packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.currencyScaleNotRead-10783.test.tsx`: a typed currency column is stored and shown at its currency's minor unit whatever its `scale`, one row per currency where the minor unit and the old `scale`-first read disagree: JPY (0) under `scale: 2`, USD (2) under `scale: 0`, KWD (3) under `scale: 2`. Control: `scale` on a `number` column still decides its stored width.
- `packages/plugin-form/src/deriveMasterDetail.currencyScale-10783.test.ts`: an identity-only column over a currency child field with `scale` hydrates to `currency`, is reported once naming the column and the child object, and stores at the minor unit (JPY, KWD). A declared currency column with `scale` is reported too. Reported once per column across two resolves. Controls: a currency column with no `scale`, and a `scale` on a column that hydrates to `number` (not reported, still decides).

The assertions name subjects (column, child object, the key), never the warning's full wording.

## Ablation

The fix was committed first. Each leg went through `ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor must hit exactly once, the blob change is verified on disk, and the restore is proven against the HEAD blob). `currencyWidth` no longer takes the column, so restoring `c.scale ??` means restoring it at each of its two callers, one leg per face. Predicted before the run: both legs turn red, each only on its own face.

| leg | mutation | red | green |
|---|---|---|---|
| stored | in `storedFractionScale`: `return c.scale ?? currencyWidth(columnCurrency(tenantCurrency));` | 4: the JPY, USD and KWD stored rows, plus the plugin-form hydrated-width pin | 9, including the `number` controls and every report pin |
| shown | in `currencyText`: `const digits = c.scale ?? currencyWidth(currency);` | 3: the JPY, USD and KWD display rows | 10 |

Both restores: blob `719fc0b8` equals `HEAD:packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx`, and `git diff HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain` were empty after each leg. The observed direction matched the prediction. No test resolves `@object-ui/fields` through `dist/`: the root vitest config aliases it to `packages/fields/src`.

## Gates

All at `587c35168`:

- `pnpm exec eslint` on the six changed TS/TSX files: exit 0, 0 errors, 52 warnings. Every warning is pre-existing `no-explicit-any`: `GridField.tsx` 27 and `deriveMasterDetail.ts` 10, the same counts as their base versions, and `GridField.test.tsx` 15. The three new or rewritten pin files add none.
  - **Declared narrowing of `pnpm lint`** (repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config` is CI's). ① Population: the diff's lintable files, each accepted by eslint's own config (the `--format json` output carries no ignored-file notice). ② Count: `--format json` reports 6 files. ③ Invariance: `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions` or `projectService` (no type-aware linting), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move the verdict on an untouched file.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0 (6 source files of 2 released packages, 1 changeset declared). `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` exit 0.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` exit 0. `pnpm check:new-line-citations` exit 0 (0 new citations). `pnpm check:shell-escape-residue` exit 0. `pnpm check:test-path-roots` exit 0. `pnpm check:installed-pin-claims` exit 0. `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` exit 0.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims` exit 0 (report-only). The one pending changeset that names a touched file, objectui#6625's, cites `.scale` reads in `GridField.tsx` as a positive control on its own base; `GridField.tsx` still reads `c.scale` for non-currency columns, so the sentence stays true.
- `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` exit 0.

An editing tool wrote the no-break-space escape in the new fields pin as the raw byte; eslint refused it as irregular whitespace. It is the escape spelling again (`587c35168`), and a control-byte and no-break-space scan over every changed file is empty.

The rest of the `check:*` farm and repo-wide `pnpm lint` are CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Where a static refusal of the hydrated case could live.** `inlineColumns` sits on the child object's own relationship field, so the sibling field a column names, and its type, are in the same object document that `os validate` judges. An object-level refinement in `@objectstack/spec` could refuse `{ name: 'amount', scale: 2 }` over a currency sibling at publish time, which this render-time report cannot. The spec's own `InlineGridColumnSchema` comment says its reach stops at the declared `type`. Raised with the dispatching seat. It is not filed here.
- **`subforms[].columns` is never judged.** `FormViewSchema.subforms[].columns` in `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0, and the `object-form` mirror in `@object-ui/types` that follows it, are `z.array(z.any())`. Measured through the public entry, `objectui validate` (the `packages/cli` source run with `tsx`): a typed currency column with `scale`, an identity-only one, and a column carrying only a bogus key each print `Schema is valid!` with exit 0, while the same document with `childObject: 5` fails with exit 1. The report added here covers the currency `scale` at render time; the column shape as a whole is unjudged on that path. Handed to the dispatching seat as a finding for the spec; not filed here.
- `deriveColumns` and `hydrateColumns` still copy a currency child FIELD's `scale` onto a computed currency column. The grid no longer reads it there, and 17.5.0 refuses `scale` on the currency field itself, so the copy is inert. Left as it is.
- `packages/plugin-form/src/deriveMasterDetail.test.ts` (the "maps a field expression to a read-only computed column" case) feeds a currency child field `scale: 2`, which 17.5.0 refuses on the field. None of its assertions read the key. Left as it is; field-level currency `scale` belongs to ruling B's FieldSchema surface, not this card.
- Producers: no example, app or doc in this repository authors `inlineColumns` or `subforms[].columns` with a `scale` (git grep over `examples/`, `apps/` and `content/`: only tests, and docs that list key names). The objectstack count (0 authored `inlineColumns` blocks declaring `type` or `scale`) is the one measured on objectstack-ai/objectstack#20045, not re-measured here.
